question: Decide whether lines to DAF-holding filers outside the DAFRC panel (non-dafrc-daf-filers-990.csv, 2,468 EINs net of top-50 sponsors) should be netted as DAF-to-DAF. Start with Marin Community Foundation's FY2022 Schedule I line of $385.7m to Dayton Foundation Plus Inc (EIN 54-2101090), the largest FY2022 recipient in the top-50 panel and a filer listed in non-dafrc-daf-filers-990.csv for FY2021-2024
conclusion_affected: FY2022 top-10/top-100 recipient shares; the netted denominator in every recipient-share study
rationale: The sensitivity that also nets these EINs lowers the FY2022 total by $1.20bn and the FY2022 top-100 share from 23.3% to 22.0%; top-10 shares move by at most 0.6 pts in any year. The repo whitelist covers only DAFRC panel EINs

question: Classify the Navigation Charitable Fund (EIN 92-1117448, NTEE U05, ruling 2023-03), which received SVCF's single $1.309bn FY2023 line, as a re-granting intermediary or an operating research organisation. Use its own 990 Part IX lines 1-3 against total expenses (the pass-through rule of b39n6-03)
conclusion_affected: Count of intermediaries among the top-50 absolute growers (16 by rule; 17 if Navigation counts)
rationale: The NTEE rule types it as a U/V research body; b40n12 calls it a re-granting intermediary. It is the #2 absolute grower and 23% of FY2023 top-10 dollars

question: Extend sponsor-cost-structure.csv daf_share_of_grants to FY2021, so recipient concentration and growth can be reported DAF-weighted for all four years
conclusion_affected: DAF-weighted FY2021 concentration; DAF-weighted growth lists
rationale: The file has daf_share_of_grants for FY2022-2025 only. For FY2022-24 DAF-weighted top-100 shares differ from filed shares by at most 0.3 pts, so the gap is small but untested for FY2021

question: Re-run the growth lists with FY2025 Schedule I lines (P1 FY2022-23 vs P2 FY2024-25) once the FY2025 itemising returns of the 44 balanced-panel sponsors are cached, to test whether the FY2023 mega-lines (JHU, Navigation, CZ Biohub LLCs) are one-off or recurring
conclusion_affected: Whether recipient concentration is rising or the FY2023 spike is transient
rationale: Top-10 share is 6.6%, 7.7%, 15.4%, 8.4% for FY2021-24 (balanced panel); the FY2023 spike is driven by a few single-sponsor lines. Two more years would separate trend from lumps

question: Read the own 990s of the 206 recipients with zero FY2021-22 top-50 DAF dollars and at least $5m in FY2023-24 (entrant rows): formation year, total contributions, and share of contributions from top-50 DAFs
conclusion_affected: How much DAF growth goes to newly formed charities rather than established ones
rationale: 77 of the 206 have a BMF ruling date in 2020 or later; 20 have no ruling (not in BMF or blank EIN). Entrants took $5.59bn in FY2023-24, 46% of balanced-panel net growth
